Any system of government, aside from direct democracy, is going to result in some group or individual having disproportionate power. All these systems will naturally lead to corruption. The big thing is that the smaller and more rigid the governing structure, the more enticing corruption becomes.

Various forms of democracy tend to lead to the most fluid and expansive government systems. These are generally going to be much more difficult to corrupt than, for instance, a king. The reason our system is particularly bad is not because of democracy, but because our form of democracy is quite outdated. Nearly all nations in the world have moved onto forms of proportional representation. In the US if a state has 100 representatives and the state is broken down perfectly even into 30% democrat, 29% republican, 21% green, 20% libertarian then that state would end up sending 100 democrats to congress. 30% of the support, 100% of the representation - that's our system. In proportional systems, that state would instead send 30 democrats, 29 republicans, 21 greens, and 20 libertarians to congress. If you get 5% of the vote then you get 5% of the representation.

So our system makes it much easier for 'establishment' powers to stay in control. We have and have had countless 'representatives' stay in office for decades largely thanks to our system. Any upstart party needs to beat every other party in an area to gain even a single seat in congress. That's the reason that even though fewer people than ever identify as democrat or republican but literally nearly every single seat at all levels of government is a democrat or a republican. Be upset at first past the post, not democracy.
